Four doors into the PPDS

The services answer different levels of the same question: monitor the market, discover the available data, interrogate it precisely, or navigate the relationships behind a procurement procedure.

Monitor

Dashboard

Indicators, trends, maps and visual reports for fast monitoring and policy analysis.

Discover

Data Catalogue

Find datasets, publishers, formats and metadata; understand what exists before analysing it.

Interrogate

Query Service

Start with prepared templates or create custom SPARQL queries for precise analytical questions.

Navigate

Graph Explorer

Follow notices, procedures, buyers, suppliers and their relationships in an interactive graph view.

PLACEHOLDER · FUTURE AI USE CASE

AI-assisted fraud / anomaly detection

From descriptive analytics to risk signals that help experts decide where to look.

Possible discussion points:

  • Which signals are useful: unusual bidder patterns, repeated relationships, timing, prices, network structures?
  • How do we make signals explainable and auditable?
  • How do we avoid turning a risk score into an automated accusation?
Principle: flag patterns for human investigation — do not equate a model signal with a finding of fraud.
Buyer A
Supplier X
Supplier Y
Procedure
Illustrative risk signal

Recurring relationship + atypical bidding pattern + contextual anomaly → review by an expert.

Concept wireframe — not a committed PPDS feature
7
Timing: 4 min
Keep this explicitly framed as a future concept: anomaly/risk signals can support investigation, not replace human assessment or constitute a finding of fraud.
PLACEHOLDER · FUTURE AI USE CASE

Query the PPDS using natural language

Let users start with a procurement question, while the system translates it into transparent, reproducible analysis.

Possible discussion points:

  • Natural language → structured query / SPARQL → result.
  • Show the query and data sources behind the answer.
  • Support follow-up questions without losing context.
  • Make uncertainty and data limitations visible.
Concept: lower the technical barrier while keeping the analytical logic inspectable.
Show me how single-bidder awards in construction have evolved in Spain since 2022 — and compare them with the EU trend.
PPDS assistant — concept response
Generated analysis would show: filters used · underlying query · source datasets · caveats.
Ask a follow-up question…
8
Timing: 4 min
Keep this as a future concept: natural-language questions can lower the barrier to PPDS querying while preserving traceability to the generated query and underlying data.

[Sources] Official PPDS Analytics page; user-requested future AI discussion topic.
Timing: 1.5 min
Use the quotations to establish why semantics matters for AI: shared meaning improves reliability and reduces the need for the model to infer the meaning of procurement data.

[Sources] Gartner Top Trends in Data and Analytics for 2026; Gartner press release, 11 May 2026; user-provided PPDS breakout-session deck, slide 11.
Timing: 2 min
Explain how the PPDS ontology gives AI systems explicit concepts and relationships. Connect each benefit to grounded, traceable answers rather than general model knowledge.

[Sources] User-provided PPDS breakout-session deck, slide 12.
Timing: 2.5 min
Show the chatbot example as a natural-language entry point to PPDS data. Stress that the system converts the question into SPARQL and should expose the query, filters and source data behind the answer.

[Sources] User-provided PPDS breakout-session deck, slide 13.
Timing: 2 min
Use the threshold pattern as an example of anomaly detection that can prompt expert review. A signal supports investigation; it does not establish fraud by itself.

[Sources] User-provided PPDS breakout-session deck, slide 14; Civio analysis linked in the source slide.
